paras: Pinoyscincus jagori, Jagor's sphenomorphus, is a species of skink, a lizard in the family Scincidae. The species is endemic to the Philippines. There are two recognized subspecies.
The specific name, jagori, is in honor of German naturalist Fedor Jagor.
The preferred natural habitat of P. jagori is forest, at altitudes from sea level to 1,000 m (3,300 ft).
Dorsally, P. jagori is brown, with darker and lighter variegations. Adults have a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of about 9 cm (3.5 in). The tail length exceeds the SVL.
Two subspecies are recognized as being valid, including the nominotypical subspecies.
Nota bene: A trinomial authority in parentheses indicates that the subspecies was originally described in a genus other than Pinoyscincus.
